summary.en: Violence in northern Ethiopia is intensifying, with the WHO warning the health system is near collapse as attacks on civilians continue, including an RPG strike near a school in Moyale that killed 60 Ethiopian Orthodox believers. Ethiopia is also conducting cross-border drone strikes, prompting Sudan to lodge formal complaints at the UN Security Council and the AU Peace and Security Council, while Kenya has begun registering over 50,000 Ethiopian refugees fleeing the Moyale clashes. The conflict has displaced 1.7 million people and affected an additional 173,000, according to UNHCR, and there were 2,824 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Vold i nordlige Etiopia intensiveres, med WHO som varsler at helsesystemet er nær kollaps mens angrep på sivile fortsetter, inkludert et RPG-angrep nær en skole i Moyale som drepte 60 etiopisk-ortodokse troende. Etiopia gjennomfører også grenseoverskridende droneangrep, noe som får Sudan til å levere formelle klager til FNs sikkerhetsråd og AUs freds‑ og sikkerhetsråd, mens Kenya har begynt å registrere over 50 000 etiopiske flyktninger som flykter fra sammenstøtene i Moyale. Konflikten har fordrevet 1.7 million mennesker og berørt ytterligere 173 000, ifølge UNHCR, og det var 2 824 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Fano insurgency
background.extract: The Fano insurgency is an armed conflict and insurgency in the Amhara Region of Ethiopia that began in April 2023 between the Fano militia and the Ethiopian government. The conflict started after the government attempted to dissolve the Amhara Special Forces and other regional forces as part of a plan to reform and centralize the country's security apparatus, and integrate them into the federal armed forces. This move led to protests and armed resistance by local forces under Fano.
